main_text.p: de Fide; quo loco sic scribit: Manifestum est prolapsus à fide, & superbia certissimum argumentum, vel reiicere aliquid eorum, quae scripta sunt, vel quicquam, quod non est scriptum, introducere; Apostolus vehementissime hoc prohibens, exemplo humani testamenti, cui nec detrahere, nec quicquam superaddere licet. [?]Itaq;, & potens omnem, & cogitationem alienam à doctrina Domini nostri semper & ubique fugiendam, monet Basilius. Deinde subiicit haec verba: Proposita siquidem, quod nunc tractamus, plurimum discrepante ab iis casibus, in quibus aliter aliquando, vel scribendo, vel dicendo praecessi fummus: quia tunc refutare haeresis, & subvertere Diabolica fraudis agebatur, nunc vero sanae fidei confessio, & simplex ac genuina manifestatio proponitur.

Haec Basilii verba, sive dicamus continuae retractationem superioris sententiae, sive ejusdem pleniorem, ac luculentiorem declarationem; illud certe constat, Basilium, utcunque in Polemicis contra haereticos, traditiones aliquando non scriptas adhibendas putarit, in controversiis tamen de fide, omnia penitus reiiciienda iudicare, quae non ex manifestis Scripturis sumuntur. Iam vero quum tam differe, tam accurate ipse mentem suam explicet; quis de Basilii sententia dubitare poterit, nisi qui veritate relicta, contentiosam obstinationem unicum sibi scopum proposuit? page.notes: The left page is grainy, with a dark stain along its left and lower edges. "Itaq;" at the start of the continuation is doubtful and is marked [?]. The word after "praecessi" is hard to read and is only approximated. The right page is cut off by the scan edge: most of its lines are missing their ends, so the fragments above are partial. The large initial D on the right page is the start of a new section, and its following words are cut off. The right-hand fragments are shown as separate lines because the scan does not allow the paragraph structure to be determined. No catchword is visible at the foot of the left page.
